question: Among the following clinical situations described, indicate which one does NOT require a thoracic drainage as the treatment of choice:

options.opa: Right primary spontaneous pneumothorax of 50% in a 30-year-old patient with a baseline saturation of 89% and pain on the right hemithorax.
options.opb: A 59-year-old man with radiological semiology of veiling of the entire left hemithorax with contralateral mediastinal shift, hypotension of 70/40 mm Hg and heart rate of 120 beats per minute, after a traffic accident.
options.opc: A 67-year-old patient with pulmonary adenocarcinoma of the distal third of the right main bronchus with extension over the intermediate bronchus with complete obstruction of the right lower lobe and middle lobe presenting dyspnea at high stress and radiological semiology of veiling of the lower third of the right hemithorax with ipsilateral mediastinal shift .
options.opd: A 45-year-old smoker with pneumococcal pneumonia of the left upper lobe and left basal hypophonosis on auscultation. Radiologically, ipsilateral pleural effusion occupying the lower third of the left hemithorax and diagnostic thoracocentesis with pH of the pleural fluid of 6.7.
